thread:
marta: Heads up — I found ~120 debug uploads to partner-error-bucket that include Vault transit ciphertext strings (format looks like "vault:v1:..."). They came from the telemetry CI debug stage between 2026-03-19 02:10 and 02:35 UTC. Likely the CI job archived raw debug artifacts without filtering. Need containment + rotation plan.

jia: yikes. Can you paste a few object keys and one sample blob (no sensitive plaintext, just the header)?

marta: sure — sample keys: telemetry-ci/pr-4824/trace-20260319-0212.log, telemetry-ci/pr-4825/debug-ctx-20260319-0230.dump, telemetry-ci/pr-4819/vault-ciphertext-20260319.bin

sample blob: "vault:v1:9b3a7f...c1e" (not the plaintext, just the wrapped token string).

sam: containment checklist (first hour):
- Remove the uploaded objects from partner-error-bucket (delete)
- Disable the CI service-account keys that ran the job
- Revoke any active Vault leases issued to that CI job/service-account
- Search audit logs for any Unwrap/Decrypt calls against our KMS/Vault transit key

Can devops-sre run deletions and key disables now?

devops-sre: doing deletes now. Commands I'm running: 
- aws s3 rm s3://partner-error-bucket/telemetry-ci/ --recursive --exclude "*" --include "pr-*" --dryrun (verify) then without --dryrun
- gcloud iam service-accounts keys disable KEY_ID --iam-account=telemetry-ci@proj.iam.gserviceaccount.com
- vault lease revoke -prefix=telemetry-ci/ (will enumerate leases and revoke)

I'll post results in ~10m.

oncall-bot: Created incident INC-2026-4321 and paged sec-oncall.

jia: also collect Cloud Audit / CloudTrail entries for kms.crypto.Decrypt / google.cloud.kms.v1.KeyManagementService.Decrypt for the timeframe. We need caller principal and destination IPs.

marta: noted — I'll run a focused log export to GCS/logs-staging/incident-4321 for analysis. Query examples: 
- GCP: gcloud logging read 'protoPayload.methodName="google.cloud.kms.v1.KeyManagementService.Decrypt" AND timestamp>="2026-03-19T02:00:00Z" AND timestamp<="2026-03-19T03:00:00Z"' --format=json > /tmp/kms-decrypt.json
- AWS: aws cloudtrail lookup-events --start-time 2026-03-19T02:00:00Z --end-time 2026-03-19T03:00:00Z --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=EventName,AttributeValue=Decrypt

sam: next: vault transit key handling. We should rotate the transit key used for wrapping and revoke the current wrapping key version to prevent future unwraps of leaked ciphertext (note: rotating transit key doesn't retroactively decrypt old ciphertext, but rewrap policy matters). Actions: 
- rotate transit key: vault write -f transit/keys/telemetry-wrap/rotate 
- set explicit rewrap policy for any long-lived objects and trigger a rewrap job for any archived ciphertext we still control
- reissue/revoke any long-lived tokens that rely on that transit key

jia: impact question — will rotating transit key break anything in prod? We only used that transit key for CI debug artifacts and staging telemetry. Confirmed?

marta: verified — telemetry CI used a different transit key in prod. This key is scoped to staging/telemetry. Low prod blast radius.

devops-sre: deleted ~118 objects (verified) and disabled 2 SA keys. Vault lease revoke returned ~7 active leases and I revoked them. Pushed audit exports to GCS.

oncall-bot: sec-oncall acknowledged incident and assigned to sam (owner).

sam: Owner next steps (24h):
1) Rotate transit key now: vault write -f transit/keys/telemetry-wrap/rotate (done after a 10m freeze window)
2) Force rewrap of any remaining ciphertext we control and scrub any offline backups referencing old ciphertext
3) Update CI job to filter artifacts and stop uploading anything that looks like vault wrappers (PR in progress: telemetry/ci#523)
4) Roll out RBAC hardening: deny PutObject to partner-error-bucket from CI SA, require a narrow write role and object-level allowlist
5) Create a follow-up runbook: how to detect "vault:v1:" strings in artifacts and block at build step (file scan)

jia: will run the audit-log analysis and attach the caller principals + IPs to INC-2026-4321. Also recommend setting an alert for any future uploads that contain the substring "vault:v1:" in object contents or metadata.

marta: communications — we should notify the partner with: what happened, objects deleted, no evidence of key unwraps so far (pending audit), and our mitigation steps. Draft message in #partnerships once sam signs off.

sam: I signed off. Draft to partner: "We discovered debug artifacts containing wrapped strings; we deleted the objects, rotated our staging transit key, and disabled the CI keys that uploaded them. We're investigating audit logs to confirm there was no unwrap. We will follow up with timeline and root cause."

devops-sre: rotation complete and rewrap job scheduled for off-peak. CI PR to sanitize uploads opened and linked in ticket.

marta: final checklist for this thread:
- [x] delete objects from partner-error-bucket
- [x] disable compromised SA keys
- [x] revoke vault leases tied to CI
- [x] rotate transit key (staging)
- [ ] confirm no KMS/unwrap events in audit logs (jia)
- [ ] push CI sanitizer to prod and enforce artifact allowlist (devops-sre)
- [ ] partner notification sent (sam)

jia: I'll close the evidence loop by EOD and post findings in INC-2026-4321.

sam: thanks everyone. Postmortem + RBAC hardening ticket will follow. :thumbsup:
